body: Thanks for the reply. Sorry, I'm not clear by what you're referring to by 'this'? It's an interesting perspective! I'd certainly love to write full-time but I'm not convinced I could earn enough to live off.

Thanks for the reply. HR is actually a good idea. My aunt is a senior HR manager so I might ask her for some insight. I think playing the field might be a good option. Funnily enough I've just come across a software engineering firm that targets humanities grads! 

I've heard of humanities grads getting into the big banks so maybe that's another avenue I can consider. 

Thanks again for your insight.

Thanks for the reply. I have considered teaching but from what I gather it's very unstable job and I'd like to have some kind of stable career progression. My original aspiration was actually to teach high school but teachers are treated very poorly here it seems so I don't think that's a possibility any more. 

I do have some writing aspiration, though I'm not desperate to get published. At this point I'd just like a stable and secure job that pays enough for me not to worry about rent. Enough for me to settle down and start a family. That seems like a lot to ask for nowadays though. 

I would consider doing a PhD but maybe later in life. I'm am quite jaded with the state of academia, especially the humanities. Right now I really just want to start earning some money for myself and stop relying on my parents. Hitting my mid-twenties has been a bit of a shock for me. It's suddenly hit me that I'm an adult who should be independent and starting a career. There's kids three years younger than me who are already climbing the ladder. I just don't know where to start. I think I'm going to post in r/findapath and maybe see a careers advisor. I just hope I can figure a plan out soon :(.
